request: Help a team triage issues and review pull requests in its repositories. Also shape the operations, so that each tool is easy for a model to call correctly.
summary: `config.yaml` passes `--dry-run`: one `github` server with 20 tools. The issue-triage tools list, read, create and update issues. They also read and add comments, list labels, add and remove labels, and list and add assignees. The pull-request review tools list and read PRs, files, commits, reviews, review comments and requested reviewers. They also request reviewers and submit a review. I left out merge, branch update, deletes and the other ~1,000 operations, so the assistant can review but can't merge or destroy anything. Widening the surface later is a one-line change in `policy.allow`. For shaping, `issues/list-for-repo` and `pulls/list` now return compact summaries (number, title, state, author, labels, assignees or reviewers, dates, URL) instead of the full GitHub payload, and they default to 30 results per page. `issues/list-for-repo` also flags which items are really PRs. The server instructions explain that every tool takes `owner` and `repo`. I replaced `auth: none` with a bearer token from the `GITHUB_TOKEN` environment variable, which needs repo access to the team's repositories. I kept the placeholder `base_url: https://upstream.invalid` as you asked, but it must be changed to `https://api.github.com` before the gateway can reach GitHub. To run it, use `openapi-mcp-gateway --config config.yaml`.
